content.title: What Time Does Coachella 2026 Start? Live Streaming Schedule For Katseye, Sabrina Carpenter, And More

Please Try Again. Powered by Reelgood Coachella is kicking off Weekend 1 with a star-studded lineup, featuring some of the biggest names in music. Sabrina Carpenter will be kicking off the first weekend of Coachella 2026 with a performance she’s described as her “most ambitious show” yet, while Karol G is set to make history as the festival’s first-ever Latina headliner. Justin Bieber will also be launching a major comeback this weekend as he takes the stage as a headliner for the very first time. The stars will be joined by dozens of acts for Weekend 1, including Katseye, Blood Orange, Geese, Taemin, PinkPantheress, FKA twigs and more. Coachella 2026 officially begins at 4:00 p.m. PDT on Friday, April 10 when Dabeull, Youna, Bob Baker Marionettes and Wednesday take their respective stages to kick off the weekend. But there are some notable absences, as well. Katseye announced Manon Bannerman will not be performing with the group this weekend. The singer announced in February she was taking a step back from the group to focus on “taking care of myself,” but HYBE confirmed ahead of the group’s debut performance that “Manon remains on hiatus,” indicating she won’t be joining the girlband when they take the Sahara stage at 8:00 p.m. PDT. The Lambrini Girls also announced they will no longer be performing at Coachella this weekend after band member Phoebe Lunny shared she fractured her neck and sustained an “acute brain injury.” The guitarist was ordered to avoid flying or performing for six weeks as they recover from the injury. Visit Advertiser websiteGO TO PAGECarpenter will be taking the Coachella stage at 9:05 p.m.PDT on Friday, April 10. But fans of the “Manchild” singer don’t have to be at the festival in order to tune in. Here is everything you need to know to livestream Coachella from home. How To Watch The Coachella Livestream: Photo: Hector Vivas/TAS23/Getty Coachella will be livestreaming every performance from every single stage this weekend on the Coachella YouTube page and the Coachella app. Consequence reports viewers will be able to stream up to four performances on YouTube at the same time in a new grid format, as well. The Coachella Stage, Outdoor Theatre and Sahara stages will also be available to stream in 4K. For fans looking to learn more about the iconic music festival, the Coachella documentary Coachella: 20 Years in the Desert is also available to stream on the festival’s YouTube channel. Viewers will also be able to tune in next weekend when the headliners return for a second performance, from April 17-19. Tags Coachella YouTube
